title: TCS Leads ₹1.54 Lakh Crore Rally as Five of India’s Top-10 Firms Gain in Market Value
excerpt: Strong Q1 earnings from India’s largest IT services company drove a ₹72,000 crore jump in its market capitalisation, powering a broader advance among blue-chip stocks despite geopolitical headwinds.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Five top Indian firms gained ₹1.54 lakh crore in market value last week.
  • TCS led the rally, adding ₹72,072 crore after strong Q1 earnings.
  • ICICI Bank and Reliance Industries also saw significant market cap increases.
  • The Sensex rose 582 points, extending recovery despite geopolitical tensions.
  • Several firms, including HDFC Bank and LIC, experienced declines in market value.

  • Five of India’s top-10 most valued companies added a combined ₹1.54 lakh crore ($18.5 billion) in market capitalisation last week.
  • TCS was the biggest gainer, adding ₹72,072 crore after reporting a 4.61% rise in June-quarter net profit to ₹13,349 crore and guiding for demand improvement.
  • ICICI Bank, Reliance Industries, Bajaj Finance and SBI also advanced, while HDFC Bank, Bharti Airtel, LIC, L&T and HUL declined.
  • The Sensex rose 582 points (0.75%) and the Nifty gained 127 points (0.52%) for the week, extending a recovery despite elevated crude oil prices and West Asia tensions.

TCS Powers the Rally

Tata Consultancy Services drove the week’s gains among India’s most valuable companies, adding ₹72,072 crore to its market capitalisation and taking its total valuation to ₹8,20,673 crore. The surge followed the company’s June-quarter results: net profit rose 4.61% to ₹13,349 crore, and management guided towards improving demand in the current quarter after disruptions linked to the West Asia crisis.

TCS closed the week with nearly 10% gains — its strongest weekly performance in months — as investors bet that the worst of the geopolitical-driven demand softness in IT services has passed.

Financials and Reliance Join the Winners

ICICI Bank was the second-largest gainer, adding ₹29,062 crore to reach a market valuation of ₹10,34,442 crore. Reliance Industries followed with a ₹23,885 crore increase to ₹17,95,091 crore, maintaining its position as India’s most valued company.

Bajaj Finance climbed ₹21,947 crore to ₹6,57,274 crore, while State Bank of India added ₹7,338 crore to reach ₹9,63,769 crore — reflecting renewed buying interest in financial stocks on the back of stable domestic fundamentals.

“Sentiment remained supported by encouraging Q1 FY27 earnings from the IT sector, renewed buying interest in financial stocks, and resilience in domestic economic fundamentals.”

— Ajit Mishra, SVP Research, Religare Broking

Five Stocks Buck the Trend

Not all top-10 firms participated in the rally. Larsen & Toubro saw the steepest decline, with its market capitalisation eroding by ₹18,098 crore to ₹5,24,841 crore. LIC lost ₹12,081 crore, falling to ₹5,48,124 crore.

Bharti Airtel’s valuation dipped ₹7,706 crore to ₹11,91,068 crore, while HDFC Bank — the second-most valued company — edged lower by ₹7,085 crore to ₹12,62,370 crore. Hindustan Unilever saw the smallest decline among losers, shedding ₹1,222 crore.

Broader Market Resilience

The BSE Sensex climbed 582 points, or 0.75%, while the NSE Nifty advanced 127 points, or 0.52%, for the week ending July 18. Markets extended their recovery despite elevated crude oil prices, heightened geopolitical tensions in West Asia and persistent uncertainty over the global interest-rate trajectory.

The current ranking of India’s top-10 most valued firms stands at: Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, Bharti Airtel, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India, TCS, Bajaj Finance, LIC, Larsen & Toubro and Hindustan Unilever.

What to Watch This Week

The coming week brings a busy earnings calendar, with several large-cap companies set to report Q1 FY27 results. Analysts say developments in West Asia, crude oil price movements and further Q1 earnings data will be the key drivers. The Sensex may test 79,200, with the Nifty eyeing a breakout above 24,500 if the current momentum holds.

For investors with India exposure, the week reinforced that domestic market fundamentals remain intact — IT earnings are recovering, banking credit growth is solid, and institutional flows continue to support blue-chip valuations even against a challenging global backdrop.
